key_insight: LongStraw enables million-token reinforcement learning post-training under a fixed GPU budget by reusing prompt computation, detaching shared state, and replaying short response branches to reduce peak training memory.
engineering_relevance: It makes long-context RL practical for AI agents that must learn from very long trajectories, tool traces, and accumulated documents without requiring proportional GPU memory growth.
method: Executes the shared prompt without autograd to avoid storing a full training graph.
Retains only the model-specific state needed for later tokens and replays response branches one at a time.
Combines the execution stack with GRPO for long-context post-training on hybrid recurrent/full-attention and compressed-attention MoE models.
evidence_signal: On 8 H20 GPUs, the system reached 2.1M-token positions for grouped Qwen scoring and response backward, with only 0.21 GB extra peak memory when increasing group size from 2 to 8, and a stress test reached 4.46M positions; on 32 H20 GPUs it validated a 2.1M-token prompt through all 78 layers of GLM-5.2.
watch_item: The reported results demonstrate execution capacity rather than full training correctness, because the captured prompt state is detached and some distributed forward and gradient composition paths are still incomplete.
paper_title: LongStraw: Long-Context RL Beyond 2M Tokens under a Fixed GPU Budget
